dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI, and test-harness orientation

evidence.note: Read run_tests.sh, run_tests.py, utils.py, filter.json to understand the harness, the three suites, the gcc-frontend constraint, and how pass/fail is scored (compile/run/exit-code). Meets anchor-5 harness reading.
Sampled multiple c-testsuite and wacc tests, explored wacc chapter/valid directory structure and expected_results.json to learn required features before coding.

SysV calling convention, stack behavior and _start/crt1 interaction were discovered reactively by inspecting generated assembly on failing test 00100 — not verified against the ABI upfront, keeping this below anchor 8.

Drilled into exact constructs (self-referential struct produces Incomplete type losing field offsets; nested -> chains) and fed diagnosis back into design — sustained investigation characteristic of the high anchors, though modeling was sometimes shallow/erroneous.

Characterized corpus by per-suite pass rate (c_testsuite 54%, wacc 61%, gcc_torture 15%) and prioritized standard-C suites over gcc-torture GCC-extensions — evidence-based prioritization, but reactive rather than upfront.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly cleared anchor 5 (thorough harness reading and multi-suite sampling) and sustained per-construct investigation of failures throughout (preprocessor, calling convention, self-referential structs, ternary), examining assembly and deriving suite-based priorities — behavior between anchors 8 and 10. But it never systematically verified ABI details against reality upfront (argument registers, alignment, struct layout were learned reactively via failing tests), and its mental models of corners were sometimes shallow or wrong, so it does not reach the full 8. This lands at a 6.

dimensions.name: Feature-staged compiler build with checkable milestones

evidence.note: Plan lists all modules and then writes the ENTIRE compiler (token, lexer, preprocessor, parser, sema, codegen, main) in one push — attempting the whole language at once rather than a dependency-ordered progression.
Second full rewrite of all modules simultaneously; still no feature-staged milestone plan with per-feature done-signals.

Reactive feature-to-feature debugging: pick a failing test (casts, chained assignment, subscript lvalue, preprocessor #if), patch, rebuild, re-run full suite. No milestone naming feature + certifying tests.
Only near-miss to staging: 'run just the c-testsuite tests to identify failure patterns' — an opportunistic subset check, not part of a planned staged sequence.
Ending tracks a single global pass rate (277/780, 35.5%) with a coarse breakdown by suite; never used per-milestone completion criteria to gate progression to the next feature.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent held a rough mental list of features/modules and tracked an overall pass rate, but it attempted the whole language at once (twice) and then debugged reactively test-by-test, with no dependency-ordered milestone plan, no simplest-first-then-layer staging, and no per-milestone success check. This matches anchor 3 (rough feature list, no explicit dependency sequencing, no per-milestone certification), sitting above anchor 0 only because of the feature list and one opportunistic subset check, and clearly below anchor 5's staged, subset-verified progression.

dimensions.name: Incremental verification beyond the final test run

evidence.note: Added a -S flag to its own compiler to emit and inspect assembly, then read the emitted asm for 00106.c to find codegen bugs (empty symbol names, %%rax double-percent escaping) — deliberately built verification infrastructure to inspect generated assembly.
Compiled 00111.c to asm with -S and ran `gcc -c t111.s` to confirm it assembles; isolated a register-width bug (movzwl into %ax vs %eax). Verifying compile success at instruction granularity.

Generated asm for 00014.c (p[0]=0 lvalue subscript), diagnosed that glv() used the pointer's storage address instead of its value, fixed only the write path — root-cause isolation via asm inspection, verifying runtime exit code.
Ran c-testsuite-only subset for faster signal than the full 780 suite, and used python scripts to categorize failures by type (43 compile fails, 92 runtime fails) to prioritize fixes.
Checked the Assign codegen handler, identified chained-assignment bug (movq %rcx,%rax lost in a rewrite), fixed and re-verified on 00011.c specifically before re-running the suite.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built a deliberate verification loop: it invested in a -S flag to inspect emitted assembly, used `gcc -c` to isolate assembly-syntax failures from runtime failures, verified both compile success and runtime exit codes on individual small test cases, ran quicker per-suite subsets, and categorized failures by root-cause type — matching the level-8 anchor closely. It falls short of 10 because it reused existing tiny test files rather than authoring minimal repros, had no reusable bisect harness or systematic asm diffing, and didn't probe edge semantics (overflow/promotion) with targeted cases; the loop was also frequently disrupted by fragile edits.

dimensions.name: Pass-count tracking and regression detection across the horizon

evidence.note: Reports score 209/780 (26.8%), notes it improved from 15.9%, and identifies 375 gcc_torture compile failures — aggregate tracking over time plus rough failure attribution used to pick next fix.

Detected regression: score dropped 294→277, suspected recent parser edits introduced regressions, ran cargo clean + rebuild to verify build integrity and re-ran suite to confirm — but only at aggregate level, never identifying which specific tests regressed.
Maintains per-suite breakdown (c_testsuite 79/146, wacc 135/221, gcc_torture 63/413) and uses the trend to decide to prioritize the closer-to-passing c-testsuite/wacc standard-C tests.

Repeatedly re-lists the same remaining bug categories (ternary, nested -> access, segfaults, GCC extensions) across many steps in prose rather than a structured ledger; does not detect its own circular re-debugging of these items.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent solidly exceeds anchor 5: it tracks aggregate pass counts over the whole build, adds per-suite breakdowns, notices when a change lowers the count (294→277), and re-runs to confirm net progress. It moves toward anchor 8 by using suite-level trends to steer where to work, but falls short of it: regressions are caught only at the aggregate level (never pinpointing which tests broke), the pass/fail 'picture by feature' is recurring prose rather than a maintained ledger, and it doesn't check for regressions after each change or catch its own repeated re-debugging of the same bugs. This places the observed behavior at 6.

dimensions.name: Revising design when an approach is falsified

evidence.note: Recognized that incremental sed-patching had corrupted parser/sema/codegen and switched approach to clean full-file rewrites — a genuine correction when the editing method was falsified, though the churn was largely self-inflicted.

Diagnosed that the lexer's newline-skipping design broke the preprocessor's directive detection and made a real representational change (added Token::Newline, changed lexer to emit newlines, parser to skip them) — adapting the design to fit a needed feature.

Repeatedly identified 'incomplete type information' as the recurring root cause behind nested ->/struct member failures, and at 431/433 attempted a resolve() fix; at 436 noted it 'apparently didn't help' — root-cause diagnosis present but the response stayed a patch rather than a redesign of the type representation.
Many full codegen.rs rewrites; several driven by sed-corruption recovery rather than design pivots, showing significant churn and a foundation that plateaued at ~277-294/780.

Detected a regression (294→277), forced a clean rebuild to verify build integrity, and reasoned about whether recent parser edits caused it — evidence of reconciling design with reality, but corrective action remained localized bug-patching.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly diagnoses root causes behind clusters of failures (newline handling, register widths, incomplete type info) and does refactor affected areas when a feature doesn't fit — matching the level-5 anchor and touching level-8 diagnostic behavior. However, when it identified the central structural limitation (no real type representation for structs/nested members) it applied an ineffective patch rather than the targeted redesign (proper type info / IR) that level 8 describes, and much of its 'adaptation' was rewrite churn to recover from its own sed corruption. This places it solidly at the mid anchor rather than higher.

dimensions.name: Extensible compiler-pipeline and representation design

evidence.note: Deliberately set up a modular staged pipeline: token.rs, lexer.rs, preprocessor.rs, parser.rs, ast.rs, sema.rs, codegen.rs, main.rs — distinct lexer/parser/analysis/codegen stages, matching the anchor-5 'coherent staged pipeline'.

Representations were improvised, not designed up front: initial AST failed to compile (Struct/Union had 2 fields where 4 needed), and Type::Func had to be reworked from Vec<Type> to Vec<(String,Type)> mid-build — shows type representation not fully anticipated.

A real lvalue vs rvalue design exists via separate codegen paths ge() (rvalue) and glv() (address/lvalue), a hard-part representation beyond anchor 5 — but its foundations had bugs (pointer subscript in glv) discovered reactively via failing tests rather than designed correctly up front.

Type-aware sized codegen with register-width helpers (ld()/rw() keyed on type size) and struct layout with size/align/offset (compute_locals) — genuine representations for the hard parts, indicating design above a bare 5.

Incomplete-type resolution (self-referential structs) was added late by threading new struct/union maps into codegen — a representational capability bolted on reactively rather than absorbed by the original design, so it falls short of anchor 8's disruption-free composition.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly cleared anchor 5: a coherent staged pipeline with distinct lexer/parser/analysis/codegen and reasonable AST/type/scope representations. It reached partway toward anchor 8 by including genuine hard-part representations — a Type enum, an lvalue/rvalue ge()/glv() split, struct layout with size/align/offset, and type-aware sized codegen. But these representations were improvised, failed to compile initially, were repeatedly reworked (Type::Func, incomplete-type resolution added late), and their rationale was reactive rather than made explicit up front, so it does not meet anchor 8's 'deliberately designed so later features slot in with minimal disruption.' That places it at a 6, between 5 and 8.

rubric.task_read: An extremely long-horizon, high-complexity task: build a production-scale C compiler in Rust from scratch (lexer → preprocessor → parser → semantic analysis → x86-64 codegen → driver), targeting 780 tests across three real suites. Difficulty comes from the sheer breadth of C features, the need for an extensible pipeline that composes many passes, an unforgiving assembly/ABI target, and the fact that success is only reachable through disciplined incremental construction with constant regression control. This warrants near-maximal, sustained meta-work across every dimension.

dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI, and test-harness orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding C semantics, the x86-64 SysV ABI, the assembler/linker interface, and above all what the 780 tests actually demand before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A compiler that guesses at the ABI, type rules, or what the test suites exercise will emit subtly wrong assembly and thrash. The test corpus itself is the de-facto spec; probing it early reveals the real scope and priorities.

anchors.0: Starts emitting code with no inspection of run_tests.sh, the test suites, expected outputs, or the calling convention.
anchors.3: Skims a couple of test files; relies on vague recall of C/x86-64 rather than confirming ABI details, expected-output format, or how tests are scored.
anchors.5: Reads run_tests.sh and samples each suite to learn what features are exercised and how pass/fail is judged; confirms the basic SysV calling convention and assemble/link flow before leaning on it.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes the corpus (which suites stress which features, distribution of hard cases like structs/preprocessor/switch), verifies ABI details (argument registers, stack alignment, struct layout, sizes) against reality, and derives a feature-priority ordering from evidence rather than assumption.
anchors.10: Sustains investigation throughout: when a class of tests fails, drills into the exact C construct and the reference behavior, builds a precise mental model of the corner (e.g. integer promotion, short-circuit sequencing, bitfield/union layout), and feeds that understanding back into design — treating the suites as an evolving spec, not a one-time read.

dimensions.name: Feature-staged compiler build with checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the compiler into an ordered progression of stages and language features, each with a concrete done-signal (a subset of tests or targeted programs it should newly pass).
dimensions.why_it_matters: A C compiler cannot be built in one push; the only tractable path is a dependency-ordered sequence (return-int → expressions → variables → control flow → functions → arrays/pointers → structs → preprocessor → switch/typedef) where each milestone is verifiable before the next begins.

anchors.0: Attempts the whole language at once or works feature-to-feature with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: Has a rough mental list of features but no explicit sequencing tied to dependencies and no per-milestone success check.
anchors.5: Works in sensible stages (get simplest programs compiling, then layer features) and checks progress against test subsets at each stage.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit dependency-ordered milestone plan where each milestone names the feature, the pipeline changes it requires, and the specific tests/programs that certify it; sequences so that foundational representation work (types, symbol tables) precedes dependent features.
anchors.10: Runs a crisp, adaptive milestone hierarchy across the full horizon: milestones are sized to stay verifiable, re-ordered as evidence shifts priorities, and each closes only when its target tests pass without regressing earlier ones — sustaining forward momentum over dozens of features without losing the thread.

dimensions.name: Incremental verification beyond the final test run
dimensions.description: Deliberately building fast, fine-grained checks — minimal C repros, per-feature test slices, inspection of emitted assembly — rather than only running the full 780-test suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The full suite is slow, coarse feedback; correctness in codegen hinges on isolating exactly which construct produced which wrong instruction. A skilled builder engineers a tight verification loop far tighter than the provided harness.

anchors.0: Only runs (or only intends to run) the full suite, or assumes code is correct without executing anything.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally but does little to isolate failures; debugging is guess-and-recompile without minimal cases.
anchors.5: Runs relevant test subsets per feature and writes small C programs to check specific behaviors, using pass counts to gauge correctness.
anchors.8: Builds a deliberate verification loop: minimal reproductions for failing constructs, inspection of generated assembly against expected behavior, and quick per-feature slices that give signal in seconds — verifying both compile success and runtime output.
anchors.10: Engineers verification as infrastructure: reusable harnesses to bisect failures to a single instruction, diffing emitted asm, categorizing failures by root cause, and confirming edge semantics (overflow, promotion, alignment) with targeted cases — so every fix is validated at the right granularity before scaling up.

dimensions.name: Pass-count tracking and regression detection across the horizon
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate, evolving picture of which features/tests pass, what remains, and catching regressions where a new feature breaks previously-passing tests.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With 780 tests and many interacting passes, adding one feature routinely breaks others; without a live done-vs-remaining ledger and regression watch, the agent circles, celebrates false progress, or silently backslides.

anchors.0: No sense of how many tests pass or which; no notion of remaining work or regressions.
anchors.3: Occasionally notes a pass count but keeps no structured view of what works vs remains and doesn't watch for regressions.
anchors.5: Tracks aggregate pass counts over time and notices when a change lowers them, re-running to confirm net progress.
anchors.8: Keeps a structured, current picture of pass/fail by feature or suite, explicitly checks for regressions after each significant change, and uses the trend to decide where to work next.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise ledger across the whole build — per-category status, newly-passing vs newly-broken after every change, and early detection of thrash/stall — using it to allocate effort to the highest-yield failures and to catch circular re-debugging before it wastes cycles.

dimensions.name: Revising design when an approach is falsified
dimensions.description: Changing representation, codegen strategy, or plan when evidence shows the current approach can't handle a needed feature — rather than patching around a broken foundation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early choices (no real type representation, register-only codegen, ad-hoc parsing) often can't support structs, sized operations, or the preprocessor; recognizing a dead end and refactoring is what separates reaching 780 from stalling at a plateau.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on a falsified assumption, repeatedly patching symptoms of a fundamentally inadequate design.
anchors.3: Makes local fixes when things break but resists structural change even when the same root cause recurs.
anchors.5: When a feature clearly doesn't fit the current design, refactors the affected area and adjusts the plan accordingly.
anchors.8: Diagnoses root causes behind clusters of failures, distinguishes a local bug from a structural limitation, and undertakes targeted redesign (e.g. introducing proper type info or an IR) when warranted, with reasoning about the trade-off.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles design with reality: anticipates where the current architecture will break, pivots decisively and surgically when an approach is falsified, and avoids both stubborn patching and needless churn — keeping the compiler on a foundation that can actually reach full coverage.

dimensions.name: Extensible compiler-pipeline and representation design
dimensions.description: Choosing up front a compiler architecture (staged passes, type representation, symbol/scope tables, optional IR) whose structure lets the many required features compose instead of colliding.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Unlike ordering (decomposition) or reacting to failure (adaptation), this is the deliberate up-front design of the artifact's internal structure. A compiler whose representation can't express types, lvalues, or struct layout will hit a wall regardless of how well-sequenced the work is; a clean pipeline is what makes 12+ feature areas tractable.

anchors.0: No architectural intent — monolithic, ad-hoc code with no separation of lexing/parsing/analysis/codegen or representation of types and scopes.
anchors.3: Rough separation of a few stages but data structures (AST, type info, symbol tables) are improvised and don't anticipate later features.
anchors.5: A coherent staged pipeline with distinct lexer/parser/analysis/codegen and reasonable representations for types, scopes, and the AST that support the planned feature set.
anchors.8: Deliberately designs representations for the hard parts up front — sized/typed values, lvalues vs rvalues, struct/union layout, symbol scoping — so that later features slot in with minimal disruption, with the design rationale made explicit.
anchors.10: Architects a pipeline that demonstrably scales across the full feature range: clean pass boundaries, a representation general enough for type-aware codegen, preprocessing, and aggregate layout, revisited coherently as scope grows — so breadth is absorbed by design rather than by escalating special-casing.
